title: Bayersdorffer's records and the Jack Tilson band
summary: He recalls the Chicago men joining Jack Tilson's band, with Herb Wiedoeft-style piano and Skinny Ennis style tenor, and recordings never issued.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Well, what about, uh, Johnny Detroit's records? Did you make any records with him?

I didn't make any records with Johnny Detroit. No? No, my brother, I don't think my brother made any of them. Mm-hmm. But he made that, uh, some, I think it was OK records or something like that. Yeah.
Well, you mentioned something about Jeanette. I thought maybe you've gotten to the Jeanette show. I, I, I, uh. Start the Anaconda.

Oh, we made a, excuse me, we made a, when we, when, when, when we left Chicago with the four men, that the first time we went, we left, after, after Spanish Ford, we had Bill Krieger, Charlie Hartman, Johnny Bieselman, myself, see. Dave Lewin and we got on piano, you should call it. Mm-hmm. I was trying to think of the guy's name, Dave Lewin. Mm-hmm. He had a band that, uh, one of those big hotels, uh, you know. Like the Pump Room or something like that. That's the way it worked. Well, anyway, he, uh, he, at that time, he, he played piano and then, then when, when he came back from Chicago, he came down to New Orleans and he stayed at my house for a while in here to work with Tony Perrani's band at the La Vida at that time. Mm-hmm. And then, uh, but then you, what was that question you asked me?
Oh, we were talking about Jeanette. Oh, Jeanette.

All right. So, so I, I have to think about this, this pianist, see. Well, anyway, when, when, when we left, left Chicago and, and joined, uh, uh, Jack Tilson with, with his band, see. We had these four men, and then we got other guys like Skinny Budd playing tennis saxophone. He used some tarryhaw and played good. He liked the way, the way, uh, oh, what's his name? He played, uh, saxophone. Don, not Don Martin. Don Martin played clarinet with Whiteman's band and Goldkiss band. But saxophone, you know, great saxophone, played tennis saxophone.
Well, so many of them. Jack Pettis, uh, Trombone.
Not Jack Pettis, but played with the rhythm kicks.
No, the white guy. He played with, uh, Gene Goldkiss band.

He played, he played, he liked the way Trombone played. He played the tenor like, like, like Trombone played the C Melodies, see? Yeah. Well, anyway, we got together. Jack, uh, Jack made a deal, and we were gonna make some rackets, see? So we took this band on, down there. But I don't know what happened to the masters. I don't know, they just never produced them, you understand?
Well, I think it did, the piano didn't record well, it's what Johnny told me, if I remember the correctly. Because it's been...
...25 years ago, Johnny told me about it.

Oh, that, that, that's the guy, uh, Wetterman. Lewinner? Wetter, Wetterman. Uh, uh, Herb Wetterman played piano with us at the time, see? Oh, I see. Because we didn't have a piano when we left Chicago.
